`getTransactionListItemKey` is defined on the `MoneyRequestReportTransactionListController` type and populated in the controller object, but it is never consumed by the only consumer (`MoneyRequestReportUnifiedList`). That component uses the module-level `unifiedListKeyExtractor` instead.

Remove `getTransactionListItemKey` from `MoneyRequestReportTransactionListController` and the corresponding `keyExtractor` function/assignment, or use `controller.getTransactionListItemKey` in `MoneyRequestReportUnifiedList` instead of `unifiedListKeyExtractor`.

The `betas` property in `BuildPolicyDataOptions` was changed from required to optional, but it is no longer destructured or referenced anywhere in `buildPolicyData`. Since the PR removed `betas` from the function's destructuring (previously at line ~2540) and from the call to `prepareOnboardingOnyxData`, this property is now dead code in the type.

Remove `betas` from `BuildPolicyDataOptions` entirely:
```diff
- betas?: OnyxEntry<Beta[]>;
```
This will also cascade through `CreateWorkspaceDataOptions` (which extends `BuildPolicyDataOptions`), ensuring callers no longer pass an unused property.

`TravelInvoicingDynamicReconciliation` receives `policyID` via the `DynamicReconciliationProps` type (and it is explicitly passed at the call site), but the component never destructures or uses it. The destructured props are `{workspaceAccountID, domainName, bankAccountList, goBack, renderReconciliationAccountSettings}` -- `policyID` is missing.

Either remove `policyID` from `DynamicReconciliationProps` and split the type so `TravelInvoicingDynamicReconciliation` only declares the props it actually uses, or use `Omit<DynamicReconciliationProps, 'policyID'>` for this component's props type.

The property `shouldRedirectToExpensifyClassic` is added to `TypeMenuSectionsParams` but is never read or referenced inside the `createTypeMenuSections` function (line 4244). The only usage is in the test file (`tests/unit/Search/SearchUIUtilsTest.ts:7082`), which passes it as a parameter. Adding an unused property to a type solely to satisfy a test caller introduces dead surface area in the interface.

The fix should go in the opposite direction: remove `shouldRedirectToExpensifyClassic: false` from the test call in `SearchUIUtilsTest.ts` rather than adding an unused property to the production type. If this property is intended for future use inside `createTypeMenuSections`, the implementation that consumes it should be added in the same PR.

`TransactionItemRowNarrowProps` is defined as `Omit<TransactionItemRowProps, 'shouldUseNarrowLayout' | 'policyForMovingExpenses'> & TransactionItemRowNarrowComputedData`, which pulls in many wide-layout-only props that the narrow component never destructures or uses: `dateColumnSize`, `submittedColumnSize`, `approvedColumnSize`, `postedColumnSize`, `exportedColumnSize`, `amountColumnSize`, `taxAmountColumnSize`, `isReportItemChild`, `isActionColumnWide`, `isHover`, `isLargeScreenWidth`, `onButtonPress`, `isActionLoading`, `shouldHighlightItemWhenSelected`, `columns`, `reportActions`, `nonPersonalAndWorkspaceCards`, and `policy`.

Define a narrow-specific props type using `Pick` that only includes props the component actually uses:
```tsx
type TransactionItemRowNarrowProps = Pick<TransactionItemRowProps,
  'transactionItem' | 'report' | 'isSelected' | 'shouldShowTooltip' |
  'onCheckboxPress' | 'shouldShowCheckbox' | 'style' |
  'isInSingleTransactionReport' | 'shouldShowRadioButton' |
  'onRadioButtonPress' | 'shouldShowErrors' | 'isDisabled' |
  'violations' | 'shouldShowBottomBorder' | 'onArrowRightPress' |
  'shouldShowArrowRightOnNarrowLayout' | 'checkboxSentryLabel'
> & TransactionItemRowNarrowComputedData;
```
This also means the parent dispatcher should construct narrow-only props instead of spreading all `sharedProps`.

`errorText` is defined in `NetSuiteSectionType` but is never set in any section item and never referenced in the rendering JSX. It is completely unused.

Remove `errorText` from the `NetSuiteSectionType` type definition since it serves no purpose in this component.

`onCancel`, `shouldNavigateAfterSave`, and `navigateBack` are declared in `DiscardChangesConfirmationProps` but are not used by `DiscardChangesConfirmation` in `index.native.tsx` (which only destructures `hasUnsavedChanges` and `onVisibilityChange`). There is also no web counterpart that could consume them, and no file imports this component.

Remove the unused fields or add the consuming code first.

The `_policyTags` parameter is added to `computeReportNameBasedOnReportAction` but is immediately marked as unused. This is dead code — the parameter is threaded through callers (`computeReportName`) and adds to the function's surface area without being consumed.

Either use the parameter in this function's implementation (if there is a modified-expense code path that should use it) or remove it until it is actually needed. Passing `policyTags` only to `computeChatThreadReportName` does not require adding it to `computeReportNameBasedOnReportAction`.

The `_policyTags` parameter is added to `computeReportNameBasedOnReportAction` but is never used inside the function body (it is prefixed with `_` and guarded by an `eslint-disable` for `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars`). This function handles action types like SUBMITTED, FORWARDED, HOLD, UNHOLD, etc. -- none of which need policy tags. The `policyTags` data is only needed by `computeChatThreadReportName`, which already receives it separately in the `computeReportName` caller.

Remove `_policyTags` from `computeReportNameBasedOnReportAction`'s signature and stop passing it from the callers:

```ts
function computeReportNameBasedOnReportAction(
    translate: LocalizedTranslate,
    parentReportAction: ReportAction | undefined,
    report: Report | undefined,
    reportPolicy: Policy | undefined,
    parentReport: Report | undefined,
): string | undefined {
```

In `computeReportName`, just remove `policyTags` from the `computeReportNameBasedOnReportAction` call:
```ts
const parentReportActionBasedName = computeReportNameBasedOnReportAction(translateLocal, parentReportAction, report, reportPolicy, parentReport);
```

The `policyTags` parameter is added to `computeReportNameBasedOnReportAction` but is never used within the function body. It only appears in the redundant guard check `if (policyTags && !parentReportAction)`, which is itself unnecessary (see related comment). The parameter is not passed to any downstream call, nor is it used for computation.

If this parameter is intended for a future PR in the migration series, consider adding it in the PR that actually uses it. Otherwise, remove it:

```diff
 function computeReportNameBasedOnReportAction(
     translate: LocalizedTranslate,
     parentReportAction: ReportAction | undefined,
     report: Report | undefined,
     reportPolicy: Policy | undefined,
     parentReport: Report | undefined,
-    policyTags?: OnyxEntry<PolicyTagLists>,
 ): string | undefined {
```

The `isAnonymousAction` prop is redundant when `shouldCheckActionAllowedOnPress={false}` is used. When `shouldCheckActionAllowedOnPress` is false, the action permission check is completely bypassed, meaning `isAnonymousAction` has no effect.

Looking at the MenuItem implementation:
```typescript
onPress={shouldCheckActionAllowedOnPress ? callFunctionIfActionIsAllowed(onPressAction, isAnonymousAction) : onPressAction}
```

The `isAnonymousAction` parameter is only passed to `callFunctionIfActionIsAllowed` when `shouldCheckActionAllowedOnPress` is true.

**Suggested fix:**
Remove the redundant `isAnonymousAction` prop:
```tsx
<MenuItemWithTopDescription
    // ... other props
    shouldCheckActionAllowedOnPress={false}
/>
```

Alternatively, if the intent is to allow anonymous access while still performing other checks, use only `isAnonymousAction`:
```tsx
<MenuItemWithTopDescription
    // ... other props
    isAnonymousAction
/>
```

The new `accessible` prop with default value `true` is added but never used in the component.

**Issue:** The prop is defined on line 84 with `accessible = true` default, but it is never passed to any of the `PressableWithoutFeedback` components in the render method. Neither the outer `PressableView` (line 126) nor the inner `PressableWithoutFeedback` (line 141) receive this prop.

**Fix:** Pass the `accessible` prop to the appropriate pressable component(s) to make the prop functional:

```tsx
<PressableWithoutFeedback
    tabIndex={-1}
    accessible={accessible}  // Add this line
    onPress={updatePressState}
    style={...}
>
```

The default value `CONST.ROLE.BUTTON` for `accessibilityRole` may not always be appropriate for this component.

**Issue:** Adding a default value means all existing uses of `CopyTextToClipboard` that were not passing `accessibilityRole` will now have `role="button"` set. However, looking at `PressableWithDelayToggle.tsx` (line 133), the `accessibilityRole` is passed through without being used in the actual pressable attributes - it only sets `accessible` and `accessibilityLabel`.

**Problem:** The `accessibilityRole` prop is accepted but never actually applied to any element, making this default value ineffective.

**Fix:** Either:
1. Remove the default value and require explicit role passing where needed, OR
2. Update `PressableWithDelayToggle` to actually use the `accessibilityRole` prop on the `PressableWithoutFeedback` component (line 141).

The new `onPress` prop added to `WorkspacesListRow` at line 513 is redundant because the same `item.action` is already being passed to the parent `PressableWithoutFeedback` at line 492.

**Issue:** The row has two nested pressables with the same action:
1. Parent `PressableWithoutFeedback` at line 487 with `onPress={item.action}`
2. Child `PressableWithoutFeedback` at line 220 in WorkspacesListRow.tsx with `onPress={onPress}`

This creates a confusing nested pressable structure where both elements trigger the same action.

**Fix:** Remove the nested `PressableWithoutFeedback` in `WorkspacesListRow` and handle the press directly in the parent `WorkspacesListPage`.
